question.text: This German is usually credited with the invention of the printing press in the mid-15th century.
question.clue: This man's invention of hand molds and an oil-based substance helped him create his most well-known invention.

swap.text: Hitler's Nazi Germany carried out this genocide during which over ten million civilians were killed. Among those targeted were Jews, Gypsies, and homosexuals.
swap.clue: The(+) Wannsee Conference was held to carry out the ultimate goal of this event which Reinhard Heydrich helped formulate.

question.leadin: According to the Venerable Bede, they invaded Britannia together with the Angles and Jutes in the 5th century.
question.text: Name these people, the namesake of upper and lower regions in modern-day Germany.
question.clue: These people were protected by forts called burhs during the Heptarchy.

swap.leadin: This city's Burgerbraukeller was the site of an uprising on November 8th, 1923 supported by Erich Ludendorff.
swap.text: Name this Bavarian city, the site of Adolf Hitler's failed Beer Hall Putsch.
swap.clue: That used in Rollerball is the BMW Headquarters and Museum.

question.leadin: This document allowed teachers to be fired indiscriminately and banned secret or unauthorized student groups.
question.text: Name these decrees that were issued following the murder of August von Kotzebue by Karl Sand.
question.clue: The enforcement of one provision forbidding the assembly of the Burschenschaften prompted Wilhelm von Humboldt to resign from politics.

swap.text: This 19th century financial crisis occurred during the presidency of Ulysses S. Grant and began after Jay Cooke failed to raise funds for the railroad industry. The Greenbacks were formed in response to this "panic".
swap.clue: Coinage legislation contributing to this event that was labeled a "crime".

question.leadin: This politician authored a report that defined 30 degrees North as the dividing line between the "prosperous North" and "developing South."
question.text: Name this man who also served as Governing Mayor of Berlin during the construction of the Berlin Wall. He was succeeded by Helmut Schmidt after an aide of his was revealed to be a spy.
question.clue: During one diplomatic trip, this man made the shocking gesture of kneeling before a memorial to the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, and he was criticized by some for agreeing to put an eastern border at the Oder-Neisse Line.

swap.text: Located on the Jutland peninsula, cities in this state include Flensburg and Lubeck, and is traversed by the Nord-Ostsee Kanal, also known as the Kiel Canal.
swap.clue: John Russell attempted to solve a dispute involving this region by convening the London Conference of 1864, whose annexation violated the earlier London Protocol of 1852.

question.leadin: This battle began when Russian commander Peter Wittgenstein attacked Napoleon's right wing near Leipzig.
question.text: Name this 1813 battle which halted the advance of the Sixth Coalition.
question.clue: The defender's left side was commanded by Heinrich Holk until reinforcements arrived from nearby Halle led by Pappenheim, who was later killed.

swap.leadin: Name these other medieval groups of knights.
swap.text: Founded in 1190 by German soldiers in the Third Crusade, they were charged with converting the pagans of eastern Europe but ended up taking political control of the region.
swap.clue: Their fortunes declined after Witold of Lithuania and Ladislav of Poland defeated an army led by Ulrich von Jungingen at a battle in Grunwald.

question.text: The Battle of Britain was spearheaded by this Nazi in charge of the Luftwaffe. In his earlier days, he founded the Gestapo.
question.clue: This man, the Commander-In-Chief of the Luftwaffe, had been a decorated fighter pilot in WWI. He is also known for the formation of the Gestapo.

swap.leadin: Name some functionaries present at the Congress of Vienna.
swap.text: Prussia was represented by Hardenberg and this man who served as a diplomat until 1819, when he decided to devote himself more to linguistics. His work is generally regarded as the basis of the Sapir-Whorf Hypothesis.
swap.clue: This former minister of education and linguist whose work foreshadowed the Sapier-Whorf hypothesis assisted Prince von Hardenburg in the Prussian delegation.

question.leadin: The first holder of this title was allowed to claim it in return for providing aid to Holy Roman Emperor Leopold I in the War of the Spanish Succession.
question.text: Give this title granted to a ruler who was nicknamed for hiring out mercenaries. To abide by German law, rulers with this title used the word "in" rather than "of" in the title until 1772.
question.answerHtml: King in Prussia [or King of Prussia or Prussian King; accept König in Preussen or König von Preussen; accept Kingdom of Prussia or Königreich Preussen; prompt on king or Frederick I “the Mercenary King”; reject “Elector of Brandenburg” or “Duke of Prussia”]

swap.text: A Lutheran confession was presented to Charles V at one of a series of diets in this city. In 1555, a treaty was concluded in this city between Charles V and the Schmalkaldic League.
swap.clue: This city, which was home to the Welser("VEL-zer") and Fugger ("FOO-gur") banking families, named a Philipp Melanchthon "Confession."

question.leadin: Answer these questions about historical figures who have much greater importance in Harry Turtledove's The War that Came Early series.
question.text: The convenient 1938 assassination of the leader of these people, Konrad Heinlein, led Hitler to make a declaration of war that is quickly matched by Daladier and Chamberlain.
question.answerHtml: Sudeten Germans [or Czechoslovakian Germans; or German Bohemians; or German Moravians; or German Silesians; or Sudetendeutsche; or Deutschböhmen; or Deutschmährer; or Deutschschlesier; prompt on “Germans”; prompt on “Czechoslovaks”; prompt on “Bohemians”; prompt on “Moravians”; prompt on “Silesians”; do not accept answers with “Slovak” used outside the context of a Czechoslovak]
question.clue: This national minority, which was expelled after the Benes ("BEN-esh") decrees, was the subject of negotiations lambasted in the book Guilty Men.

swap.leadin: Name these banking families in European history.
swap.text: Working closely with the Hapsburgs, this German family of crediting and mining interests was ennobled by Maxmilian and then financed the election of Charles V as Holy Roman Emperor.
swap.clue: Archduke Sigismund granted a member of this family control over Tyrol's silver mines after that member of this family loaned Sigismund a huge number of florins.

question.leadin: This document stated that its purpose was to put forth a common declaration on behalf of the Lutheran, Reformed, and United churches.
question.text: Identify this document drafted at its namesake synod which condemned the teachings of the "German Christians" for imperiling the German Evangelical Church.

swap.leadin: The namesake of this ship was assassinated in Davos by David Frankfurter, who, when asked why he did it, said "I fired the shots because I am a Jew."
swap.text: Name this ship that was sunk by a Soviet submarine in 1945. 9,400 Germans on board it drowned, many of them civilians, resulting in the largest loss of life by a single ship sinking in history.
swap.clue: This ship, named after an assassinated Nazi leader from Switzerland, was built as the flagship of the Strength Through Joy cruise fleet. The most deadly shipwreck in history occurred when this ship was sunk by a Soviet submarine while evacuating German civilians.

question.leadin: This man's forces won a critical victory at the Battle of Tanga, which saw swarms of bees descend on the attackers on the slopes of Kilimanjaro.
question.text: Name this "Lion of Africa," who led a small band of Askaris and German soldiers on a guerilla campaign against hundreds of thousands of Allied troops before finally surrendering, undefeated, at the end of World War I.
question.clue: Another member of this family was the final Republican opponent of extending the PATRIOT Act after filling defeating John Conway and Trey Grayson to fill Jim Bunning's Senate seat.

swap.text: This German commander wiped out the Hereros as commander in chief of German South West Africa, by cornering them into the Kalahari Desert, and poisoning their water Kefka-style.
swap.answerHtml: Lothar von Trotha (Adrian Dietrich Lothar von Trotha)
swap.clue: This military figure responsible for much the genocide that killed civilians and soldier alike at the Battle of Waterburg.
